title: Rethinking the Sampling Criteria in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning: A Competence-Difficulty Alignment Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing instantaneous single-step pass rates against accumulated historical performance to demonstrate the variance and statistical bias in estimating the true difficulty of mathematical reasoning problems.

Conducting an ablation study by removing the uniform warm-up sampling phase to measure the algorithmic impact of overrepresenting certain common problem types (e.g., algebra) and marginalizing unseen topics during early reinforcement learning.

Substituting standard sample-level loss calculations with a token-level policy gradient loss in the objective function to prevent the reinforcement learning model from being biased by response lengths.
